title: "Design Lab: Ad Click Event Aggregation"
---

# Design Lab: Ad Click Event Aggregation

Build a Go event-ingestion API and minute-window aggregator using synthetic clicks. The key distinction is event time (when a click occurred) versus processing time (when the worker saw it). Retries and delayed delivery make the two diverge.

## Ingestion and state

`POST /clicks` accepts a bounded batch of `(event_id, ad_id, occurred_at)`. Authenticate the producer and validate timestamp bounds. A success response means the events reached the declared durable log boundary, not merely a Go channel.

Keep raw events under a retention policy and store aggregates by `(ad_id, window_start)`. For the baseline, deduplicate event IDs and increment the affected aggregate in the same database transaction. A unique event ID plus an independent counter update is insufficient if a crash can separate the two.

Bucket event time in Go with UTC:

```go
func minuteStart(t time.Time) time.Time {
	return t.UTC().Truncate(time.Minute)
}
```

Import `time`. Specify half-open windows `[start, start+1 minute)`. The timestamp at exactly the next minute belongs to the next window.

## Late data and replay

Choose a five-minute allowed lateness for the lab. Maintain a watermark with an explicit source policy, such as the minimum active partition progress minus tolerated disorder. Handle idle partitions deliberately; taking the maximum across partitions can finalize slow partitions prematurely.

For a simpler first milestone, use server-time cutoffs and name that policy accurately. Return provisional counts until the cutoff. Route later events to a correction path or a rejected-event store; do not silently drop them. Finalization means “closed under this policy”, not proof that no more real clicks exist.

Partition by ad ID for per-ad ordered processing, then introduce a deliberately hot ad. Salting a hot key spreads load, but requires a second-stage combine and another deduplication boundary. Keep sketches or approximate counters out of a contract that promises exact totals.

## Go worker and recovery

Use bounded fetch batches and transactions with context deadlines. Commit consumer offsets after aggregate transactions complete. Replay from a retained raw log into a new aggregate version for backfills, then atomically switch the query version. Dedupe retention must cover the replay horizon; expiring dedupe rows early can double-count old clicks.

## Acceptance evidence

Feed events out of order, duplicate a batch, crash after transaction commit but before offset commit, and test the exact minute boundary. Assert the deduped total is unchanged by replay. Inject an event beyond the lateness limit and verify the documented correction or rejection behavior.

Report ingestion lag, watermark delay, duplicates, late events, and hot-key throughput. Compare final aggregates against an offline exact computation over the synthetic fixture. Use the [queue design lab](../../18-distributed-infra/153b-distributed-message-queue.qmd) to explain which guarantees belong to the broker and which belong to this consumer.
